subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures stay in the accepted-then-async run path with a visible terminal startup-failure state, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight sandbox startup before returning `accepted`?
rationale: The choice affects the public `sessions_spawn` timing contract, lifecycle phase vocabulary, gateway waits, and session/subagent projections rather than a local Docker error string only.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` accepting the child run, but emit and project a typed startup failure that updates logs, session state, and subagent status when sandbox startup fails.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accepted
options.body: Resolve or validate sandbox startup before returning `accepted`, giving immediate errors at the cost of stricter spawn latency and behavior.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle tracker
options.body: Keep this as the sandbox proof case while the broader lifecycle issue decides the `first-progress` and `startup-failed` event contract.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` accepting the child run, but emit and project a typed startup failure that updates logs, session state, and subagent status when sandbox startup fails.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points most strongly to steipete across sandbox inheritance and subagent lifecycle ownership boundaries.
